decoded_evidence.note: Class I: these fields name what the bytes ARE and rest on an external layout, so they are capped below the literal layer whatever the offsets are. The primitive half is in literal_reads[]. Two independent methods: (1) the field order and every mask read from the first-party UE 5.4.4 source at the build's own changelist, cited per field; (2) the file's own packed layout plus the independent copy of the flags byte in each local entry header, neither of which reads the index bitfield. The two agree: 0 of 2 entries carry Flag_Encrypted in the index, the layout probe returns SUPPORTS_PLAINTEXT, and the local-header probe found 0 disagreements.

payload_policy: D-02. A payload is read only from an entry whose Flag_Encrypted bit (IPlatformFilePak.h:382, read per IPlatformFilePak.cpp:7174) is CLEAR. No key is derived, searched for or used, and no decryption is attempted. When every entry is encrypted this tool reads no payload at all and reports that as the finding.

plaintext_proofs.reasoning: bEncryptedIndex is 0 and SHA1 over the 138 bytes as they sit on disk equals the hash stored for this blob, so DecryptAndValidateIndex (IPlatformFilePak.cpp:6489-6500) would take its no-decrypt path and accept exactly these bytes. Reading them is therefore reading plaintext, not decrypting.

bEncryptedIndex is 0 and SHA1 over the 32 bytes as they sit on disk equals the hash stored for this blob, so DecryptAndValidateIndex (IPlatformFilePak.cpp:6489-6500) would take its no-decrypt path and accept exactly these bytes. Reading them is therefore reading plaintext, not decrypting.

encoded_blob_tiling.what_this_probe_can_refute: the whole bitfield layout. Wrong field widths cannot tile a blob exactly by accident.

entry_flag_word_census.what_this_probe_can_refute: a wrong mask. A summary hides a mask error; a census cannot. If the encrypted bit were really the low bit of a wider method field, the method values here would not be nameable from the footer table.

layout_probe.what_this_probe_can_refute: the encrypted verdict, without consulting any flag. An encrypted uncompressed entry occupies Align(Size, 16) bytes on disk and an unencrypted one occupies Size, so the two hypotheses predict different files.

local_header_probe.what_this_probe_can_refute: the index bitfield decode. The local header is a second copy of the same flag, written by a different serializer at a different place in the file; a wrong mask would disagree with it.
local_header_probe.why_these_bytes_are_plaintext: the packer writes this header with FPakEntry::Serialize and encrypts only the payload buffer (PakFileUtilities.cpp:2736 vs :1057/:1109), and the bytes read here carry Offset 0 and Size/UncompressedSize equal to the index for every header read. Ciphertext would not.

readable_within_d02.note: No payload byte was read by this run. Under D-02 a payload may be read only from an entry whose Flag_Encrypted bit is clear, and 0 of 2 entries have it set.

summary.what_this_does_not_settle: whether the cooked packages in the IoStore containers use unversioned property serialization. This pak holds no cooked package at all, so CK-01 cannot be answered from it either way.
